title_en: Yang Mingji, Lin Shouru — smuggling case
keywords_en: criminal; smuggling; second instance; death penalty review; Supreme People's Court; High People's Court; Intermediate People's Court; Guangdong Province; state organ; Supplementary Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Punishment of Smuggling Crimes; Criminal Law; whether it is smuggling by a unit; determination of principal and accessory offenders; whether the sentencing is appropriate; affirm the original judgment; armed smuggling; cigarette smuggling; border guards committing crimes in law enforcement
full_text_en:
Yang Mingji and Lin Shouru — Smuggling Case

Defendant Yang Mingji, male, 34 years old, formerly Deputy Captain of the Sanzao Border Defense Brigade of the Border Defense Division of Zhuhai Public Security Bureau, Guangdong Province, arrested on August 24, 1993.

Defendant Lin Shouru, male, 29 years old, formerly an officer at the Nanshui Border Defense Police Station of the Border Defense Division of Zhuhai Public Security Bureau, Guangdong Province, arrested on August 24, 1993.

The Zhuhai People's Procuratorate, Guangdong Province, instituted a public prosecution against Defendants Yang Mingji and Lin Shouru for the crime of smuggling before the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court, Guangdong Province.

The Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court, after trial, found:

During the period when Defendant Yang Mingji served as Deputy Captain of the Sanzao Border Defense Brigade of the Border Defense Division of Zhuhai Public Security Bureau, Guangdong Province, and was responsible for anti-smuggling work, in order to seek exorbitant profits, in or around February 1993, he conspired with smugglers Kuang Jianzhong, Chen Guangxian, and Lin Jianyi (all separately prosecuted) to engage in smuggling, agreeing to secretly transport cigarettes from Macau to Sanzao, Zhuhai, for sale by smugglers Huang Zhunan and others (separately prosecuted). Yang Mingji was to dispatch personnel and speedboats to escort the cigarette-laden vessels to the Sanzao dock and collect escort fees. Yang Mingji also rented the vessel "Zhu San Yun 06014" for loading cigarettes with Kuang Jianzhong in Wanzai, Zhuhai. Subsequently, Yang Mingji colluded with Defendant Lin Shouru, and under the pretext of carrying out official duties at sea, assigned police officers Zhang Jiehua, Zhang Bin, and Xiao Guicai (all separately prosecuted) to wear police uniforms, carry firearms, and drive a speedboat to the waters near the Jiu'ao Deepwater Dock in Macau to meet and provide armed escort for the vessel carrying smuggled cigarettes to the Sanzao dock. Between March 8 and March 28 of the same year, Yang Mingji led Lin Shouru and police officers Zhang Jiehua, Zhang Bin, and Xiao Guicai on four separate occasions to smuggle a total of 2,300 cartons of cigarettes, with a total value of RMB 5,175,000, and he personally obtained illegal proceeds of RMB 48,200. Defendant Lin Shouru participated in armed escort of smuggling activities on five separate occasions between March 8 and April 3 of the same year, involving a total of 2,900 cartons of cigarettes, with a total value of RMB 6,525,000, and he personally obtained illegal proceeds of RMB 43,300. After the case was discovered, Defendant Yang Mingji returned illegal proceeds of RMB 20,000, and Defendant Lin Shouru returned illegal proceeds of RMB 42,800.

The above facts are confirmed by physical evidence including the seized vessel "Zhu San Yun 06014" used for transporting smuggled cigarettes and the speedboat used for escorting smuggled cigarettes, documentary evidence, and witness testimony.

The Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court held: Defendants Yang Mingji and Lin Shouru, as state public security and border defense personnel, during the period when they were responsible for anti-smuggling work, for the purpose of obtaining illegal gains, violated the law they were supposed to enforce, contravened customs regulations, and by taking advantage of their official positions, provided armed escort for smugglers to smuggle cigarettes. Their conduct constituted the crime of smuggling as provided in Article 4, item (1) of the Supplementary Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress Concerning the Punishment of Smuggling Crimes (hereinafter referred to as the "Provisions"). Yang Mingji played a role in planning and organizing the joint smuggling crime; according to Article 23 of the Criminal Law, he is the principal offender in this case and shall be given a heavier punishment according to law. Lin Shouru played a secondary role in the joint smuggling crime; according to Article 24, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, he is an accessory in this case, and pursuant to paragraph 2 of the same Article, he shall be given a mitigated punishment compared to the principal offender. Defendant Yang Mingji committed the crime of smuggling, and the value of the goods he escorted in smuggling was particularly huge, and the circumstances are particularly serious. He shall be punished according to Article 4, item (1) of the Provisions, and his personal property shall be confiscated. According to Article 53, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, Yang Mingji is sentenced to deprivation of political rights for life. Defendant Lin Shouru committed the crime of smuggling, and the value of the goods he participated in escorting in smuggling was huge. Considering that he is an accessory in this case, he shall be given a mitigated punishment compared to the principal offender Yang Mingji according to Article 4, item (1) of the Provisions, and his personal property shall be confiscated. According to Article 53, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, Lin Shouru is sentenced to deprivation of political rights for life.

Accordingly, the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on November 1, 1993:

1. Defendant Yang Mingji is convicted of the crime of smuggling and sentenced to death, with deprivation of political rights for life, and confiscation of personal property amounting to RMB 80,000.

2. Defendant Lin Shouru is convicted of the crime of smuggling and sentenced to life imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for life, and confiscation of personal property amounting to RMB 30,000.

3. The illegal proceeds returned by Defendant Yang Mingji, RMB 20,000, and by Defendant Lin Shouru, RMB 42,800, are to be confiscated and turned over to the State treasury.

After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, Defendant Yang Mingji appealed to the Guangdong High People's Court on the grounds that the smuggling was conducted on behalf of his unit, and Defendant Lin Shouru appealed on the grounds that he participated in the armed escort under the direction of Yang Mingji, requesting a lighter punishment.

The Guangdong High People's Court, after trial, held: Regarding Appellant Yang Mingji's claim that the cigarette smuggling escort was for the benefit of his unit, upon investigation, when he proposed to the unit leader about escorting cigarette smuggling for the unit's profit, he was immediately stopped by the leader. However, he persisted in his own course, unilaterally colluded with smugglers to jointly plan cigarette smuggling, sought exorbitant profits, and was the leader in organizing personnel for armed escort of smuggling activities. His individual criminal conduct of cigarette smuggling is confirmed by the testimony of co-defendants and other evidence. Yang Mingji's denial of individually escorting cigarette smuggling lacks factual evidence, and his grounds for appeal cannot be established. Lin Shouru requested a lighter punishment on the grounds that he participated in the escort smuggling under the direction of Yang Mingji. Upon investigation, Lin Shouru actively participated in armed escort of smuggling activities, sought exorbitant profits, and should have been severely punished. Considering that he was an accessory, the first instance had already imposed a mitigated sentence. His current appeal requesting further leniency lacks sufficient reason and is not accepted. The facts found in the first instance judgment are clear, the evidence is reliable, the conviction is accurate, the sentence is appropriate, and the trial procedure is lawful. Accordingly, on December 13, 1993, pursuant to Article 136, item (1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court ruled to reject the appeals of Appellants Yang Mingji and Lin Shouru and affirm the original judgment.

Pursuant to Article 144 of the Criminal Procedure Law, the Guangdong High People's Court submitted the criminal ruling affirming the first instance judgment sentencing Defendant Yang Mingji to death with deprivation of political rights for life to the Supreme People's Court for approval.

The Supreme People's Court, after review, ruled on February 24, 1994, to approve the criminal ruling of the Guangdong High People's Court affirming the first instance judgment convicting Defendant Yang Mingji of the crime of smuggling and sentencing him to death with deprivation of political rights for life.
